reviewHistory.summary: P0 was zero: cross-tenant write blocking, DML-only credentials with 1142 denials, no cross-schema grants, 20 of 20 artifact digests, 58 checks reproduced and the gates and 1429 regression all green were independently confirmed. The findings were about accounting rather than missing work.

The four first-round P1 findings were confirmed closed: the reviewer independently re-ran 23 of 23 gated classes and recomputed 46 of 46 digests. One new P1 was raised, that the gated runner's pass criterion was the mvn exit code, which an entirely skipped class also satisfies, and which propagated into VERIFIED and a green gate. Ten P2 findings were raised as well.

The third round closed the second round's new P1 and seven of its ten P2 findings. It returned REWORK on three new P1 findings: a ledger exit-evidence item judged NOT_APPLICABLE with a hardcoded PASS standing in for it, three numbers in the canonical manifest that did not match their evidence, and drift during the review, since building workflow-service for M2-006 made the evidence package unable to rebuild itself at the commit it named. P0 remained zero and the review independently reproduced the core runtime facts: DML-only credentials refused with error 1142, cross-schema denial, the Redis ACL scoping, and the migration histories.

Not submitted. The mechanical findings of the third review have been addressed: the generator's four literal statuses are now derived from measurements, three disputed numbers are corrected with their definitions, the reproduction command carries its opt-in, and the stale wording and figures in the surrounding documents are aligned. Whether the rollback and compensation test belongs to this task or to M2-006 is a question about task boundaries and is awaiting the human decision, so that entry reports NOT_APPLICABLE.

results.details: Twelve owners provisioned; each can read its own schema; the eleven externally migrated owners are DML-only with DDL and ALTER denied by privilege (error 1142); SHOW GRANTS names no foreign schema.
Every owner was probed against three other owners and every read was denied; the exhaustive declaration check is the grant listing, which names only the owner schema.

Every owner the policy gives a Redis namespace was probed, 16 in total including the two that have no database schema, and each resolved to exactly one ACL user scoped to its own namespace, able to write inside it and refused in another owner's. The requirement's second clause is covered separately: the business fact row counts in thirteen owner tables were identical before, during and after Redis was stopped and restarted, so losing Redis cannot create or lose a business fact.

Twelve schemas have a p1r_schema_history whose version set matches the migration files; applying V1 into an empty scratch schema created all five expected tables; invalid SQL was rejected with no residue.

Delivered at the storage layer. 10 *TenantIsolationTest classes run against a real MySQL, each against its own owner's schema, writing and reading facts with a JdbcTemplate and asserting that a foreign tenant's rows are not returned; all 10 pass when run with their flags. MEASURED, WITH ITS DEFINITION, because the figure moves with the method: counting `new <imported com.englishflow production class>(` in each test's source, 6 of the 10 instantiate at least one production class and 4 do not (AssessmentTenantIsolationTest, GamificationTenantIsolationTest, NotificationTenantIsolationTest, SocialTenantIsolationTest). Counting any import from a service package instead gives 8; counting any reference including static calls gives more. So this is evidence about schema-level isolation, and it is not evidence that every service's request path enforces the same rule. The HTTP-level two-tenant negative is residual and needs the synthetic per-owner account P1R-M0-007 builds and P1R-M2-009 wires into CI.

13 *FlywayMigrationTest classes run emptyAndExistingDatabasesMigrateAndFailureRecovers against a real MySQL, one per service including audit-service, and all 13 pass. That is what makes the ledger's "including audit-service" phrasing true rather than an inference from version reconciliation.
A projection rebuild entrypoint belongs to the workflow and platform runtime in P1R-M2-006; content cache invalidation belongs to P1R-M3-006.

P1R-M2-006 scope: workflow Saga, compensation, scheduled jobs and manual recovery, which produce the owner, trace, audit and recovery receipts this requirement asks for. The ledger exit evidence phrase "rollback/compensation test" is carried by that task.

P1R-M6-008 implements account deletion requests, the cooling-off period, withdrawal, cross-domain anonymisation and the final subject state; P1R-M8-012 drills retention and deletion. This single owner is also what config/p1r-m2-requirement-owners.v1.json records, so the earlier disagreement with the execution record is gone.
Redis was stopped (unhealthy) and restarted (healthy), and the row counts of 14 durable business tables were identical before, during and after.

The gateway contract schema identifier is 37 characters while both schema_version columns were VARCHAR(32). Because the receipt insert used INSERT IGNORE, MySQL truncated the value into a warning and stored a corrupted receipt while the fact insert failed outright. The widening is read from the migration that performs it, requiring both columns to reach VARCHAR(64). The endpoint behaviour is read from the tracked check `scripts/runtime/verify-audit-ingest.mjs`, which mints a short-lived RS256 token, ingests one event and replays it: first ingest accepted observed 202; replay is a duplicate observed 200; one receipt observed 1; one fact observed 1; schema identifier stored whole observed m2.gateway.security-audit.evidence.v1; column wide enough observed 64

P1R 1435/1435 with 0 failures and 1435 passing, read from evidence/p1r/m2/P1R-M2-004/regression.json; the full suite reports 1930 tests with 0 failures. The twenty-four legacy B failures that were pre-existing are fixed and each fix strengthened the assertion rather than relaxing it.

rollbackEvidence.details: Checked against the migration files rather than asserted: 62 migrations across the owners were scanned for DROP COLUMN, DROP TABLE, RENAME and any MODIFY that narrows a column. 0 contain one, so reverting the commits restores the previous schema shape without losing data.

Measured by the harness: with a recorded migration checksum corrupted, the reconcile runner for learner_service exited 2 and refused with "owner schema reconciliation failed: learner-service migration V1__create_learner_service_schema.sql changed after it was applied". The record was then repaired in a finally block, so a failed assertion cannot leave a false checksum behind, and the runner converged again with exit 0. The recorded checksum was confirmed restored afterwards: true. This is the rollback and compensation evidence the ledger line names, and it is owned by this task rather than reassigned.

knownGaps: The tenant guard is delivered at the storage layer through 10 passing *TenantIsolationTest classes, each running against a real MySQL and its own owner's schema. They write with a JdbcTemplate rather than through a service repository, and four of the ten reference no production class at all, so they show that each schema isolates its tenant's rows; they are not evidence that every service's request path enforces the same rule. The HTTP-level two-tenant negative remains open and is handed to P1R-M2-009: it needs a synthetic per-owner account, which P1R-M0-007 builds and P1R-M2-009 wires into real CI. P1R-M2-009's ledger scope does not itself name tenant guard, so this is a residual gap recorded against this task rather than a reassignment of the requirement.

The per-service Redis namespaces and ACLs are provisioned and probed for every namespaced owner, but no domain service uses Redis yet: only api-gateway and the legacy core-api configure it, so for the twelve domain owners the namespace is a reserved allocation rather than an enforced boundary in a live path.
The owner outbox tables now carry the contract shape, but only content-service has a publisher and a consumer; the other owners still append rows that nothing publishes.

Eight of the twelve provisioning owners were baselined from an existing schema rather than migrated from empty, so their migration history records what was already applied rather than a replay from scratch. The empty-database drill is covered separately by the Flyway tests above rather than by those baselines.

p1r_schema_history, written by scripts/database/reconcile-owner-schemas.mjs, is authoritative for the eleven externally migrated owners and records the version and checksum the reconcile runner applied. flyway_schema_history belongs to the service that runs Flyway at startup, which is iam-service today, and to the service-owned tests. They are not interchangeable: the reconcile history is what the platform asserts, and a Flyway history exists only where a service or its tests actually ran Flyway.

The four gated test families in this task are unchanged in themselves; what changed is that they are now run on purpose. A default `mvn test` still reports them as skipped, so any future evidence that cites them has to run scripts/runtime/run-gated-db-tests.mjs.
nextSteps: Two independent reviews have returned REWORK, so a third one has to re-decide this submission; the implementer changed the harness, the evidence generator and a governance check during the rework and must not accept its own output.

Whether the rollback and compensation test belongs to this task or to P1R-M2-006 is a question about task boundaries: the ledger line for this task names it, while config/p1r-m2-requirement-owners.v1.json assigns it to M2-006. That entry reports NOT_APPLICABLE until the human decides, and the decision should be reflected in the ledger text rather than only in the config.

The workflow-service built under P1R-M2-006 is now a provisioned owner, which changes the owner count this evidence describes. Its schema, credential and tenant guard are delivered by that task, not by this one, so this task's snapshot should either be re-measured on a revision that includes it or state that boundary explicitly.
